title: Jorge Martín Leads Austrian GP After Spectacular Sprint Victory
seoTitle: Jorge Martín leads Austrian GP after sprint win
subtitle: Saturday's race at the Red Bull Ring brings a championship twist to the 2026 MotoGP season
excerpt: Jorge Martín won the Austrian GP sprint, recovering from 8th to take the MotoGP World Championship lead. The main race kicks off at 9 AM.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Jorge Martín secured victory in the Austrian GP sprint race and, by ending Saturday as the World Championship leader, has sparked significant fan interest. The main race is scheduled for Sunday, at 9 AM (Brasília time), at the Red Bull Ring in Spielberg.

How the Sprint Race Unfolded at the Red Bull Ring

Martin started from pole position, lost ground, and dropped to 8th place before beginning a recovery that took him to the top of the podium. The sprint victory was celebrated alongside Marc Márquez and Francesco Bezzecchi, who completed the podium.

Recovery That Secured the Lead

After Ácosta's fall, who was leading the sprint, Martin advanced consistently, overtaking rivals in the final laps and crossing the finish line in first place. This performance allowed him to take the lead in the world championship.

Sunday Session Schedule

The main MotoGP race begins at 9 AM (Brasília time) and will be broadcast on ESPN and Disney+. Moto2 has its race at 7:15 AM, Moto3 at 6:00 AM, and the Bagger World Cup features two races, the first at 3:55 AM.

Weather Conditions Forecast for the Race

According to weather.com, the day will be cloudy, with a maximum temperature of 24°C and a minimum of 12°C. Winds are expected to be around 5 km/h, humidity around 44%, and no rain is forecast for the race time.

What to Expect from the Main Race

With Martin's newly acquired lead, the battle in the main race promises to be intense. Final adjustments to the bikes are made just before the start, and riders are already showing confidence in the stable weather conditions.

With information from MotorSport.com.br, www.motogp.com.
